title: Natural projection to the two-term naive cotangent truncation
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $P\twoheadrightarrow B$ a surjective $A$-algebra map, where $P$ is a polynomial $A$-algebra on any set of variables or a localization of such an algebra. Put $J=\ker(P\to B)$ and $C(P)=[J/J^2\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}\Omega^1_{P/A}\otimes_P B]$ in degrees $-1,0$, where $\mathrm d([h])=\mathrm dh\otimes1$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. For the standard cotangent complex [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] in $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there is a canonical map $L_{B/A}\to C(P)$ inducing an isomorphism $\tau_{\geq-1}L_{B/A}\simeq C(P)$. Truncation means replacing degree $-1$ by the cokernel of the incoming differential and discarding degrees below $-1$. This comparison is natural under commutative diagrams of such surjective presentations: a compatible map $P\to P'$ over $A\to A'$ and $B\to B'$ gives the semilinear chain map $C(P)\to C(P')$, with $[h]\mapsto[h']$ in degree $-1$ and $\mathrm dp\otimes b\mapsto\mathrm dp'\otimes b'$ in degree $0$, and it commutes in the derived category with the standard functoriality map on $L$. No vanishing below degree $-1$ and no finite generation of the differential module is asserted.

source.place: Tags 08RB (lemma-relation-with-naive-cotangent-complex), 08UP (remark-explicit-comparison-map); arbitrary polynomial presentations: algebra.tex Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy) and equation-functoriality-NL; localization: Tag 00S7 (lemma-localize-NL) and cotangent.tex Tag 08SF (lemma-localize).

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] with $R=A[B]$, augmentation $\epsilon:R\twoheadrightarrow B$, $I=\ker\epsilon$, and $Q_1=A[R]$, $Q_2=A[Q_1]$. Denote their respective polynomial variables by $X_b,Y_p,Z_f$. Write $M_n=\Omega^1_{Q_n/A}\otimes_{Q_n}B$, with $Q_0=R$. The two faces on $Q_1$ send $Y_p$ to $p$ and $X_{\epsilon(p)}$. On $Q_2$ the three faces send $Z_f$ to $f,Y_{d_0f},Y_{d_1f}$. Thus $L_{B/A}$ is represented by $\cdots\to M_2\xrightarrow{\partial_2}M_1\xrightarrow{\partial_1}M_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables], $M_1$ is free on $u_p=\mathrm dY_p\otimes1$ and $M_2$ is free on $\mathrm dZ_f\otimes1$. These are precisely the standard-resolution faces, not faces for an arbitrary presentation.

source.place: Tag 08UP (remark-explicit-comparison-map): standard resolution and face maps; Tag 08QL functoriality.

proof.text: Define $D:Q_1\to I/I^2$ by $D(f)=d_0(f)-d_1(f)\bmod I^2$. Both face maps have the same image in $B$, so the difference lies in $I$. It is additive, kills $A$, and satisfies $D(fg)=\overline fD(g)+\overline gD(f)$ because the product of two face differences lies in $I^2$. Hence [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] gives a $B$-linear map $\rho:M_1\to I/I^2$, $\rho(u_p)=p-X_{\epsilon(p)}\bmod I^2$. Its composition with the conormal differential is $\partial_1$: both send $u_p$ to $\mathrm dp-\mathrm dX_{\epsilon(p)}$. Moreover $\rho(\partial_2(\mathrm dZ_f))=D(f)-D(Y_{d_0f})+D(Y_{d_1f})=0$: the last two terms subtract $d_0f-d_1f$ since $\epsilon d_0f=\epsilon d_1f$. Thus degree zero identity, degree minus one $\rho$, and zero in all lower degrees form a chain map $c:L_{B/A}\to C(R)$.

source.place: Tag 08UP: well-definedness and the omitted verification that the displayed arrows form a complex map.

proof.text: We compute $E=M_1/\operatorname{im}\partial_2$ explicitly. Let $t_p$ be the class of $u_p$. For each $f\in Q_1$, the defining relation is the class of $\mathrm df\otimes1$ minus $t_{d_0f}$ plus $t_{d_1f}$ equal to zero. In particular $f=Y_{X_b}$ gives $t_{X_b}=0$ for every $b\in B$. Taking $f=2Y_0$ gives $t_{2X_0}=-t_0$, and $f=Y_0^2$ gives $t_{X_0^2}=t_0$. For $h,k\in I$, the choices $f=Y_h+Y_k$ and $f=Y_hY_k$ now give $t_{h+k}=t_h+t_k-t_0$ and $t_{hk}=t_0$. These identities follow by differentiating the displayed polynomials using the Leibniz rule [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]; their coefficients are evaluated in $B$, so the coefficients $\epsilon(h)$ and $\epsilon(k)$ in the product derivative vanish.

source.place: Tag 08UP: explicit calculation of the cokernel of the incoming differential; details supplied for the omitted truncation verification.

proof.text: For $r\in R$, $h\in I$, set $b=\epsilon(r)$. The relations for $Y_rY_h$ and $Y_rY_0$ yield respectively $b t_h-t_{rh}+t_{X_bX_0}=0$ and $b t_0-t_0+t_{X_bX_0}=0$. Subtracting gives $t_{rh}-t_0=b(t_h-t_0)$. Together with Step 3 this says that $h\mapsto t_h-t_0$ is additive, is $R$-linear with the $R$-action through $\epsilon$, and kills $I^2$ (each product of two elements of $I$ maps to zero). It therefore defines a $B$-linear map $v:I/I^2\to E$. This uses just quotient-module relations and the computed identities, with no regular-sequence or finiteness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 08UP: inverse to the induced degree-minus-one comparison, first half of the direct calculation.

proof.text: The induced map $\overline\rho:E\to I/I^2$ is inverse to $v$. Indeed, for $h\in I$ one has $\overline\rho(t_h-t_0)=(h-X_0)-(0-X_0)=h\bmod I^2$. Conversely let $p\in R$ and $b=\epsilon(p)$. For $f=Y_p-Y_{X_b}$ the defining relation of $E$ becomes $t_p-t_{X_b}-t_{p-X_b}+t_0=0$. Since $t_{X_b}=0$, this reads $v\overline\rho(t_p)=t_p$. The $t_p$ generate $E$, so both composites are identities. Therefore $\rho$ identifies $M_1/\operatorname{im}\partial_2$ with $I/I^2$ and intertwines the remaining differential with the conormal differential by Step 2. The degree-zero identity then makes $\tau_{\geq-1}L_{B/A}\to C(R)$ an isomorphism of the displayed two-term complexes. Its construction commutes strictly with ring squares: $X_b,Y_p,Z_f$ map to the variables indexed by their images, and every formula above commutes with those maps.

source.place: Tags 08RB/08UP: direct completion of the canonical truncation comparison; no transitivity compatibility is left unproved.

proof.text: For a surjection $P\to B$ as in the statement, put $C(P)=[J/J^2\to\Omega^1_{P/A}\otimes_PB]$. Any map $a:R\to P$ over $B$ induces a chain map $C(a)$: on conormal classes it sends $[h]$ to $[a(h)]$, and on differential tensors it sends $\mathrm dr\otimes b$ to $\mathrm da(r)\otimes b$. The map on conormal quotients is well defined since $a(I^2)\subset J^2$; the map on differentials follows from [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and the two maps commute with the differential on each $[h]$. These formulas work also for semilinear maps over a base-ring square, preserve identities, and compose termwise. A lift $a:R=A[B]\to P$ exists: choose a preimage in $P$ of each $b\in B$ and apply [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Algebra Tag 00S0 (section-netherlander), equation-functoriality-NL and the generator-lifting argument of Tag 00S1.

proof.text: For later independence and inverses, the following difference calculation applies to maps of these complexes, including semilinear maps. Suppose $a,b:Q\to T$ over the same ring square and quotient $B\to B'$ induce the same map to $B'$, and $K=\ker(T\to B')$. Then $a-b$ modulo $K^2$ is a derivation into the $B'$-module $K/K^2$: $a(xy)-b(xy)=a(x)(a(y)-b(y))+(a(x)-b(x))b(y)$. By [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] it gives $H:\Omega^1_{Q/A}\otimes_QB\to K/K^2$, $H(\mathrm dx\otimes b_0)=b'_0[a(x)-b(x)]$. On conormal generators $H\,\mathrm d([h])=[a(h)-b(h)]$, and on differential generators $\mathrm dH(\mathrm dx\otimes b_0)=b'_0(\mathrm da(x)-\mathrm db(x))$. Thus $C(a)-C(b)=\mathrm dH+H\mathrm d$. The same calculation is valid for maps into $T/K^2$, interpreting differentials after tensoring with $B'$: $\mathrm d(K^2)\otimes B'=0$ by the Leibniz rule. This also verifies independence of lifts represented only modulo a squared ideal.

source.place: Algebra Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy), explicit difference derivation and both homotopy identities, including its omitted calculation.

proof.text: If $P$ is polynomial, [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentations-homotopy-equivalent] makes $C(a):C(R)\to C(P)$ a homotopy equivalence for any lift $a$. For the allowed general case write $P=W^{-1}F$, $F=A[x_e]$. Lift the images of $x_e$ in $B$ to $R/I^2$ by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. This makes $D=R/I^2$ an $F$-algebra, with square-zero ideal $N=I/I^2$, and $D/N=B$. The given map $P\to B$ is an $F$-algebra map. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-localization-square-zero-lifting] yields $\ell:P\to R/I^2$ lifting it. Since $\ell(J)\subset N$ and $N^2=0$, $\ell$ induces a map $J/J^2\to I/I^2$. The derivation $\mathrm d:R\to\Omega^1_{R/A}\otimes_RB$ vanishes on $I^2$, so it descends to $R/I^2$ and, composed with $\ell$, gives the degree-zero map by [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. These maps form a chain map $C(\ell):C(P)\to C(R)$.

source.place: Algebra Tag 00S1 (lemma-NL-homotopy); localized polynomial comparison using Tag 04EG (lemma-localization-formally-etale) via the cited square-zero lifting leaf.

proof.text: The two composites in Step 8 are homotopic to identities by Step 7. On $R$ compare $\ell a:R\to R/I^2$ with the quotient map; they have the same reduction to $B$, and induce $C(\ell)C(a)$ and $1_{C(R)}$. In the other direction $a$ descends to $\bar a:R/I^2\to P/J^2$. Compare $\bar a\ell:P\to P/J^2$ with the quotient map; they induce $C(a)C(\ell)$ and $1_{C(P)}$. Thus $C(a)$ is a homotopy equivalence also when $P$ is a localization. Step 7 also says that all choices of $a$ give the same map in the homotopy category, hence the same map in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Composing the canonical map $c$ of Steps 2–5 with $C(a)$ now defines the required canonical morphism $L_{B/A}\to C(P)$, independent of every lift. It induces the asserted isomorphism on truncations, since Step 5 identifies the truncation with $C(R)$ and $C(a)$ is a homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Tag 08RB/08UP and Algebra Tag 00S1: derived comparison via mutually inverse presentation maps; localized case supplied by Step 8.

proof.text: Finally consider any given diagram $A\to A'$, $B\to B'$, $P\to P'$. Put $R'=A'[B']$ and choose lifts $a:R\to P$, $a':R'\to P'$. Let $s:R\to R'$ be the standard map $X_b\mapsto X_{b'}$. The composites $R\xrightarrow{a}P\to P'$ and $R\xrightarrow{s}R'\xrightarrow{a'}P'$ have the same reduction to $B'$. Step 7 gives a semilinear homotopy between their maps $C(R)\to C(P')$. The canonical comparison $c$ commutes strictly with the standard resolution map by Step 5 and [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Composing that strict square with this homotopy proves the required naturality square in the derived category (the target is regarded as a $B$-complex by restriction of scalars). The map $C(P)\to C(P')$ is exactly the formula of Step 6, including for localized presentations. This proves all naturality assertions. The calculation only quotients $M_1$ by $\operatorname{im}\partial_2$; it makes no claim on the lower cohomology or any finite generation.
